## Overview
A concise lecture-style summary of multivariate optimization focusing on derivative-based and numerical methods.

## Learning goals
- Understand gradient and Hessian concepts for multivariate functions.
- Apply second-order tests to classify critical points.
- Implement Newton and Quasi-Newton methods for optimization.
- Formulate constrained problems using Lagrange multipliers.

## Outline
- Definitions: f(x), ∇f(x), H(x)
- Second-order conditions and tests
- Multivariate Newton's method (derivation and algorithm)
- Line search and step-size selection
- Quasi-Newton methods (BFGS overview)
- Constrained optimization: Lagrange multipliers (brief)

## Examples and code
- Two-variable example comparing Newton and BFGS (R/Python)
- Use optim()/scipy.optimize.minimize for practice

## Homework
- Read Givens & Hoeting (Part I, Section 2.2) and work the example on p. XX.
- Apply BFGS to the Rosenbrock function and report convergence behavior.

## Resources
- Lecture notes can be found at ODTUClass: https://odtuclass2026f.metu.edu.tr
- Givens, G. W., and Hoeting, J. A. (2013). Computational Statistics (2nd ed.). Wiley.
